slides.heading: Remove Kth Node From End
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Remove Kth Node From End, a medium linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Remove in place (list length >= 2, k valid).
If the head is removed, the head node takes its successor's value so the reference stays valid.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Remove in place (list length over equals 2, k valid). If the head is removed, the head node takes its successor's value so the reference stays valid.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Keep a gap of k between two pointers so the leading one hits the end when the trailing one is just before the target.
slides.narration: Keep a gap of k between two pointers so the leading one hits the end when the trailing one is just before the target.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Two passes: count length, then walk to n − k
One pass with a k-gap between two pointers
slides.narration: Two passes, one to count and one to walk, works fine. The single-pass trick keeps two pointers exactly k apart, so when the leading one reaches the end, the trailing one is right before the target.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Move both until the lead ends
3. Unlink the target, handling the head
slides.narration: Step by step. First, advance the lead k steps. Second, move both until the lead ends. Third, unlink the target, handling the head.

slides.caption: Move fast 4 steps ahead
slides.narration: Move fast 4 nodes ahead, so the gap between fast and slow is exactly k.

slides.narration: Move both together. Slow is at 2, fast at 6.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Advance both: slow at 5
slides.narration: Move both together. Slow is at 5, fast at 9.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: slow.next = slow.next.next removes 6
slides.narration: Fast is at the last node, so slow is just before the k-th from the end. Skip over 6 to remove it.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Fast moves k steps. If it's null, the head is the target, so we overwrite the head with its next. Otherwise we advance both until fast is the last node and skip slow's next.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Removing the head (k = length): copy next into head
Stop fast at the last node, not null
slides.narration: Removing the head is the special case: fast becomes null, so we copy the second node into the head and skip it.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: return the new head instead
slides.narration: Using a dummy node avoids the head special case. Mention it.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Keep a gap of k between two pointers so the leading one hits the end when the trailing one is just before the target.
slides.narration: To recap Remove Kth Node From End: Keep a gap of k between two pointers so the leading one hits the end when the trailing one is just before the target. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
